resolutions.researcher_notes: This is the row's own seed citation (RBN Energy, 'Floodin' Down In Texas', Housley Carr, 10/16/2016) -- the live URL now 403s (bot-blocked, not confirmed dead), so proposing the Wayback capture (2021-09-26 snapshot) instead, per the brief's rule to add a snapshot rather than treat a block as a deletion. The article states: 'most intrastate systems were built in the 1960s and '70s to deliver Texas production to Gulf Coast industrial consumers during the period of federal price controls.' This is a GENERAL statement about the Texas intrastate-pipeline industry's build-out era, not a claim naming Enterprise's system or 'Texas Intrastate System' specifically -- gem.wiki's own page cites this exact article for its 'Start Year: 1960s' entry, and the sheet's StartYear1=1960 reads as the first-year-of-decade convention for that same '1960s' figure. Given the source only supports a decade-level approximation for the broader industry rather than a system-specific date, tier is LOW rather than medium, independent:false (one source). Searched and ruled out: Enterprise Products' own investor-relations 'Natural Gas Pipelines & Services' page (2022-09-25 Wayback capture) and its FY2023 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, adsh 0001061219-24-000006) both describe the Texas Intrastate System in operational/ownership detail but contain no construction or in-service date at all (no '1960' or 'built in' language anywhere in either document) -- Enterprise's own asset descriptions are silent on system age. FERC eLibrary and RRC records were not checked further because this is an intrastate gathering/transmission SYSTEM (an aggregate of many historic pipeline segments acquired and consolidated over decades, per the 10-K's own footnotes describing partial/undivided interests), not a single certificated interstate line with one in-service order -- a single 'birth date' for the whole aggregated system is unlikely to exist in FERC records and none was found. CONCERN: none on this unit -- 1960 is presented on the sheet as an approximate/decade-anchor value consistent with how the industry and GEM's own wiki page already describe it, not a specific claim in tension with any source found.

Enterprise Products Partners L.P.'s own asset table (both on its investor-relations 'Natural Gas Pipelines & Services' page, Wayback 2022-09-25 snapshot -- the live URL now 404s -- AND its FY2023 Form 10-K filed with the SEC, 2024-02-28, CIK 0001061219) name 'Texas Intrastate System' by its exact GEM name and list 'Enterprise' / Enterprise Products Partners as Operator. The IR page states: 'The remainder of our Texas Intrastate System is wholly owned' (after carving out a leased portion of the Wilson storage facility). The 10-K's asset table lists the Texas Intrastate System's Ownership Interest as 'Various' with footnote (5): 'We proportionately consolidate our undivided interests, which range from 22% to 80%, in 1,469 miles of the Texas Intrastate System' -- out of the system's total 6,719 miles, meaning roughly 5,250 miles (~78%) is wholly (100%) owned by Enterprise and the remaining ~1,469 miles is a partial/undivided joint interest at 22-80% depending on the segment. Both documents are Enterprise's own statements (one publisher, different venues) -> medium/not independent, not high. Treated as REFS_ADDED (not a full match) because the value is directionally and substantially correct -- Enterprise IS the sole operator and the clear majority owner -- but the sheet's blanket 'Owner1% = 100.00%' is a simplification of a more nuanced structure with a real minority undivided-interest carve-out. CONCERN: the Texas Intrastate System is NOT uniformly 100% Enterprise-owned end to end -- per Enterprise's own FY2023 10-K footnote (5), about 1,469 of its 6,719 miles are proportionately-consolidated undivided interests ranging 22%-80% (i.e., partially owned with unnamed co-owners), while the remaining ~5,250 miles are wholly owned. This does not contradict Enterprise being the correct Owner1/operator of record, and no source names a specific second owner entity to add as Owner2, so no value change is proposed -- flagging for awareness only, since a future editor with access to the segment-level breakdown may want to split this network-level row's ownership more precisely. Searched and ruled out: the annualreports.com-hosted 'NYSE_EPD_2022.pdf' seed citation is a confirmed dead link (live URL 404s, and Wayback's availability API returns no snapshot for that exact path) -- superseded here by the SEC's own EDGAR-hosted FY2023 10-K, which is the authoritative primary-source version of the same annual-report content and covers the identical asset table.
